labelChirho: therefore, for this reason, on this account
descriptionChirho: The adverbial phrase ki 'al ken meaning 'therefore, for this reason, on this account' — a causal/inferential conjunction linking a reason to its consequence; Arabic هٰذَا (hadha) 'this' and ذٰلِكَ (dhalika) 'that' used deictically to point back to the stated cause; Korean 까닭에 (kkadak-e) 'for the reason' and 그렇게 (geureoke) 'so/thus'; Spanish así/esto 'thus/this'; Hindi कारण (kaaran) 'reason' and इसलिए (isliye) 'therefore'; Swahili hivyo 'thus' and kwa hiyo 'therefore.' Both clusters represent the identical causal adverb with no semantic distinction — the 7-occurrence cluster and the 2-occurrence cluster differ only in minor translational variation across target languages, not in underlying Hebrew meaning. All 9 occurrences function as discourse connectors establishing cause-result relationships.
